html:
The Medes were an ancient Iranian people of northwestern Iran, around their capital Ecbatana, today's Hamadan. Assyrian records first name them in the 800s BCE, as many small chiefdoms that paid tribute to Assyria.

Like the Persians, they came from Iranian-speaking herders who had moved onto the plateau. Herodotus says they were united into one kingdom, and that under King Cyaxares they drove back the Scythians, then joined Babylon to destroy Assyria, sacking Nineveh in 612 BCE. Their power reached into Anatolia, where a war with Lydia ended after the eclipse of 585 BCE stopped a battle. They may also have ended Urartu.

In 550 BCE Cyrus the Great of Persia, by tradition the grandson of the Median king Astyages, overthrew him and took Ecbatana. The Medes became the second people of the Achaemenid Empire, and Greeks often called the Persians "Medes". Media stayed a province, and its north later became the kingdom of Atropatene. How large and organised the Median "empire" really was is still debated.
